summary: Security review found one concrete account-enumeration risk in login timing; JWT validation, password derivation, token storage, and task authorization otherwise meet the intended local-app design.

messages.content: Security follow-up: _login returns immediately when a username is absent but runs PBKDF2 for existing users, creating a measurable username-enumeration timing difference if the server is exposed. Run PBKDF2 against a fixed dummy salt/hash before returning the same 401 response for unknown users.

Security sign-off is pending a small login timing-enumeration mitigation. All other reviewed controls are present: random salts with PBKDF2, required environment secret, strict HS256 validation with constant-time HMAC comparison, sessionStorage-only frontend token handling, and user-scoped task mutations.

blockers: Login timing distinguishes unknown usernames from known usernames because only known users execute the 310,000-iteration PBKDF2 verification.
decisions: Do not expose this unauthenticated-by-default server beyond localhost until login timing is equalized and additional abuse controls are considered.
Continue rejecting malformed/expired tokens and returning 404 for cross-user task mutations to avoid resource-existence disclosure.
